#163251. Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (989 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (989 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements.
  • In a recent development, after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux.
  • It has been revealed that ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.

In a recent development, after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it’s an installable package with automatic updating.

It has been revealed that ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google’s Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird’s rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. “The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday’s announcement. “The browser around it is modest, but functional.”.

In a recent development, nearly the entire modern web at the moment runs on three browser engines. There’s WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that’s where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.

An independent implementation of web standards has value not just by providing additional competition in the market, but because it can’t help but reveal places where sites depend on Chromium behaviors rather than published specifications. The fact that Ladybird exists isn’t likely to shift the market tides any time soon, but every latest browser engine increases the number of implementations that standards can be tested against, which can surface Chromium-specific assumptions and push the ecosystem toward the spec.

The Ladybird project was borne out of Kling’s SerenityOS project, an attempt to develop a new independent OS from scratch, before splitting off as a separate project. Kling formed the Ladybird Browser Initiative, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by sponsorships and donations. The project’s site highlights that there are no sponsored search engine deals supporting the project like many other popular browsers, and sponsoring entities have no say in the project roadmap.

The Ladybird alpha is a rolling release channel that updates automatically, and the downloadable package is a huge step to getting the browser onto the PCs of everyday users. “Ladybird improves quickly, and until now you had to build it from source to see that,” Kling wrote. Though the browser began as C++, in keeping with the ethos of SerenityOS, the project has since started shifting toward Rust, starting with its JavaScript engine.

It has been revealed that while it’s exciting to have a fresh engine option for browsing, the project leader notes that this is still a very early release. The browser build contains a built-in tool for reporting any websites that fail to render or crash the browser. Kling writes, “We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today.”.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft consumers are still out in the cold on this one for now. The project says that future support for Windows is planned, but it’s macOS and Linux only for now.

I tested the Ladybird alpha version 2026.47.8 on my AceMagic W1 mini PC AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS with 16GB DDR5 and running Fedora Linux 44 with the newly introduced KDE Plasma 6.8.3, and the most surprising thing about the alpha build was how little it feels like alpha software.

Sources indicate that the browser seemed to handle most anything I threw at it without problem. Day-to-day tabbed browsing mechanics felt snappy and normal. A 50MB test video file downloaded quickly and smoothly. With a dozen tabs open, switching between them was instant, and the browser felt responsive throughout. Options menus were surprisingly fleshed out for a build this young.

Google Maps loaded instantly, located me, and handled everything I threw at it: adding and removing layers, zooming out from the Midwest, and dropping into Street View in Alberta, Canada in around three seconds. Everything rendered fast enough that my mini PC’s fan spun up noticeably. GitHub’s site, including repository navigation, worked without a hitch. So did YouTube and the news sites I tried.

According to recent reports, I could stall the browser, but it took some effort. With about 10 tabs open, I was streaming a 4K test video file from my personal Jellyfin server. Everything worked fine at first, but after skipping around in the file over and over again, the browser eventually got stuck. Mind you, this is an alpha build that I was trying to trip up, not a representation of something inherently broken.

After spending an evening with Ladybird, I can say that while it won’t be replacing Firefox for me anytime soon, I was genuinely impressed that a scratch-made engine could perform this well in such an early state. Most newly introduced browser projects are forks of something that already exists. Ladybird is the rare exception, an engine written from nothing, and the alpha runs well enough that if you have a Mac or Linux PC handy, it’s worth downloading a build and poking around yourself. Just remember Kling’s warning: This is nowhere near trustworthy enough to make your daily driver, yet.

According to recent reports, what the alpha demonstrates is that a small team of independent developers, funded by donations, has built a browser engine from scratch that handles real web browsing without a fuss. That it works this well this soon, using no existing engine code, is an achievement. I thought I was a Firefox loyalist, but I’ll be keeping an eye on where this one goes.

French minister under fire for Playboy magazine cover

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • French government minister Marlene Schiappa has come under fire from members of her own party after appearing on the front cover of Playboy magazine.
  • In a recent development, schiappa, who has been a government minister since 2017, appeared on the cover of the magazine to accompany a 12-page interview she did on women’s and LGBT rights.
  • Schiappa has been a long-time advocate for women’s rights and was appointed as the country’s first ever Gender Equality Minister in 2017.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

French government minister Marlene Schiappa has come under fire from members of her own party after appearing on the front cover of Playboy magazine.

In a recent development, schiappa, who has been a government minister since 2017, appeared on the cover of the magazine to accompany a 12-page interview she did on women’s and LGBT rights. Schiappa, who is the current Minister for the Social Economy and French Associations, was photographed for the cover wearing a white dress.

Schiappa has been a long-time advocate for women’s rights and was appointed as the country’s first ever Gender Equality Minister in 2017. In this role, she successfully spearheaded a new sexual harassment law which allows for on the spot fines to be issued to men who catcall, harass or follow women on the street.

Her appearance has drawn criticism from political colleagues including French Prime Minister Elisabeth Borne.

Borne pulled up Schiappa over the cover, telling her it “wasn’t appropriate, especially during this period,” CNN affiliate BFMTV reported Saturday, citing a source close to the prime minister.

France is presently in the throes of a political and social crisis triggered by French President Emmanuel Macron’s move to push ahead with controversial pension reforms despite widespread public opposition.

“We are in the middle of a social crisis, there is the issue of policing, there are people between life and death, and I have the impression of being behind a smoke screen,” Sandrine Rousseau, Green Party politician and fellow women’s rights activist, told BFMTV Friday.

France wracked by more pension protests amid rising violence on the streets.

French politician, Jean Luc Mélenchon who came third in the 2022 presidential elections criticized both Schiappa’s appearance and the decision by French President Emmanuel Macron to give an interview to children’s magazine, Pif Gadget, this week.

Industry observers note that “In a country where the President expresses himself in Pif and his minister in Playboy, the problem would be the opposition. France is going off the rails,” Mélenchon tweeted Saturday.

Schiappa responded to her critics in a tweet on Saturday, saying: “Defending the right of women to have control of their bodies, that’s everywhere and all the time. In France, women are free. With all due respect to the detractors and hypocrites.”.

French Interior Minister, Gérald Darmanin came to Schiappa’s defense during an interview with French news channel CNews on Sunday calling her a “woman of character.”.

“I wanted to say that Marlene Schiappa is a courageous female politician who has her character and who has her style which is not mine, but I respect,” he remarked.

  • A handful of earnings reports on Tuesday pointed to a mix of factors behind the strong results, including a resilient consumer, stronger execution and demand for the right products at the right price.
  • In a recent development, kohl's reported comparable sales growth of 1.2% for the period ended Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once-struggling retailers are entering the holiday quarter with improved performance and sales momentum as turnaround efforts begin to resonate with shoppers.

A handful of earnings reports on Tuesday pointed to a mix of factors behind the strong results, including a resilient consumer, stronger execution and demand for the right products at the right price.

In a recent development, kohl's reported comparable sales growth of 1.2% for the period ended Oct. 31 and raised its full-year outlook as CEO Michael Bender said customers "have remained resilient" but are "migrating to value with their purchases.".

He tied improvement to the manufacturer's work on product assortment, store experience and value.

Best Buy also on Tuesday posted its highest comparable sales growth in five years, at 6.1%, which prompted the electronics retailer to raise its full-year outlook.

In a recent development, "We have a tremendous amount of momentum," CEO Jason Bonfig told CNBC in an interview. "The fact that we saw pretty much broad-based growth across almost all of our categories is a lot of momentum that we're very excited about.".

The firm also credited execution, market share gains and a compelling product cycle alongside growing customer demand.

Sources indicate that at Dick's Sporting Goods, quarterly comparable sales rose 2.6% at the core business and 0.5% at Foot Locker. CEO Lauren Hobart remarked "all income demographics grew" and the organization "didn't see trade-down from best to better or better to good.".

She similarly pointed to newly introduced products and market share gains within the category as contributing to the strong quarter. She also highlighted continued improvement at Foot Locker.

All three companies have been undergoing efforts to boost sales and get the right products on shelves to meet customer demand.

Recent findings suggest that target, likewise undergoing revitalization efforts, last week reported comparable sales growth of 5.6% in the third quarter, fueled by a 5% increase in comparable traffic. The retailer raised its full-year outlook.

CEO Michael Fiddelke at the time called the traffic gain "a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often.".

Even Gap CEO Richard Dickson told CNBC the company has moved from "rebuild mode" to "turnaround mode" at its Old Navy banner, a sign of progress, albeit not a broad-based portfolio recovery.

In a recent development, michael Baker, a retail analyst at D.A. Davidson, told CNBC he sees both a resilient consumer and firm-specific improvements as driving sector strength.

According to recent reports, "Retail sales have been more resilient than most think," Baker said. His analysis showed retail sales, excluding autos and gas, rose 5.1% in the third quarter on a nonseasonally adjusted basis — the strongest quarter since the pandemic.

But he cautioned that growth appears to be coming more from transaction size than traffic, with inflation, promotions and higher units per transaction driving up spend.

Dollar Tree, which reported better-than-expected earnings on Tuesday morning, posted a 3.8% increase to traffic, accelerating from 0.4% growth in the prior quarter, suggesting more shoppers may be bargain hunting. Comparable sales at the retailer increased 4.6% during the period.

Sources indicate that "Consumers are under pressure, and they are increasingly selective about where and how they spend," stated Dollar Tree CEO Michael Creedon on the company's earnings call. "When under pressure, shoppers prioritize value and buy closer to need.".

Comparable sales of everyday essentials rose 8.9% at Dollar Tree stores in the third quarter, while sales of nonessential items were essentially flat, the company remarked.

— CNBC's Laya Neelakandan contributed to this report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that my house has been powered by Alexa and Amazon devices to some degree for the past decade. There's always an Alexa somewhere in my house, ready for a quick command, and it's an ecosystem I find myself coming back to again and again—especially since Amazon always has something new coming out to catch my eye.

While not everything is on sale from Amazon's various ecosystems (sorry if you've got an eye on one of the newest Kindles; those have yet to be on sale), there are several great Amazon devices you can get for a better price than ever during Black Friday. Here are all the best deals I've found on Amazon devices.

Looking for more discounts? Don't miss our guide to the Absolute Best Black Friday Deals. Hunting for Kindles and e-reader deals specifically? I've got a story for that, too.

Sources indicate that this is my latest bedside companion. The Echo Time feels more like a second-generation Echo Spot than the actual Echo Spot that came out two years ago; I'm curious why they didn't just make this a third-gen Spot. The Echo Time brings back the larger screen of the original Echo Spot and has a fun range of customizable clock faces you can use. It has sleep sensing to wake you up in the half-hour window before your official alarm time. You'll have to place it perfectly for that feature to work, but I've liked it a lot more than I expected. It also has no camera, so you can put it in your bedroom without any worries. It's expensive for what it is, so now is a great time to pick one up for yourself.

It has been revealed that if you want an Amazon speaker that's small with plenty of sound power, the Echo Dot Max takes the small form of the long-popular Echo Dot and adds better sound and a smart-home hub. It even acts as a Wi-Fi extender if you're an Eero user. The price is great, too, for all you'll get.

It has been revealed that looking for something small but more affordable? The fifth-generation Echo Dot has improved sound over the older Dot models (though this one's getting up there in years, too) and has one of the cheapest price tags you'll find for a good Alexa-powered speaker.

In a recent development, if you want an Amazon-powered speaker with the best sound, the Amazon Echo Studio is always the answer. The original Echo Studio was my pick for sound quality, and the second generation still is. It also has a built-in smart home hub with Omnisense technology, spatial audio, and Dolby Atmos, and it can double as an Eero Wi-Fi extender.

Industry observers note that the best of Amazon's latest generation of smart displays is the Echo Show 11. The Echo Show 8 is usually my go-to, but I think the Show 11 is worth the extra money for its bigger screen and better sound. It also has a built-in smart home hub, but it won't double as an Eero extender like the Studio or Dot Max.

As an avid note-taker, I love the Kindle Scribe. It's my go-to device to bring on a plane in case I get the itch to write a list or brainstorm an idea, while also knowing I could switch over to read my latest library book all in one device. The newer Kindle Scribes have been hard for me to recommend with the high price tag, but right now the third-gen Scribe is actually cheaper than the older second-gen model. I also really like the homepage design on the newer Scribes.

It has been revealed that if you're looking to upgrade your e-reader experience, try a color Kindle. The first-generation Kindle Colorsoft is on sale, letting you add color highlights and see your book covers in full color (though a little muted since it's an e-paper screen). It's been hard to recommend because of the price and the lack of other features besides the color screen, but this deal price is pretty great, since it's actually a little cheaper than the older model for once.

You can also get a better price on an even bigger color screen with the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft. It's on sale for a massive discount during Black Friday—$180 off—and adds a color screen to all the features you'd already get on the newest Kindle Scribe. It's a great device, though it does have a shorter battery life due to the color screen (Amazon rates it for up to eight weeks of reading or two weeks of writing). It’s only $50 more than buying the older, no-color second-gen model I've long loved.

If you're looking for the classic best Kindle to buy for a lower price, it's the Kindle Paperwhite. The newer version isn't on sale, but the 12th-gen version from 2024 is still great at an unbeatable price. You could spend a little less by buying the 2024 basic Kindle on sale, but I think the larger screen, a warm-toned front light, and longer battery life are well worth the extra cost. You can also get the Signature version on sale, but I wouldn't splurge on the older Signature, as the newer Signature will be compatible with Amazon's newest Kindle accessories, like the page-turn case.

According to recent reports, if you want to control more things with your Echo speaker, these compact smart plugs from Amazon let you turn various devices in your home into voice-controlled ones. The plugs are a little expensive normally, but $15 per plug is a solid deal, so you can pick up a few of these for things like lamps.

These smart bulbs aren't Amazon-branded, but they are compatible with Amazon's smart home ecosystem. I love Cync's bulbs best out of all the ones I've tested, and you can get a two-pack for less than $30 during Black Friday sales.

Recent findings suggest that one of my all-time favorite smart devices is a smart lock. If you want one that looks good without costing an arm and a leg, the Aqara Smart Lock U50 is the one I recommend. You will need a hub to let it have Wi-Fi and work with Amazon's smart home ecosystem, though.

If you want a TV powered by Amazon, our latest favorite from Amazon's lineup is actually its art TV. The Ember Artline is our favorite TV in Amazon’s lineup. Samsung’s The Frame feels more premium, but our team found the Artline plenty capable for displaying artwork, and it costs much less. It's a great option to get an art TV on a budget, especially during Black Friday.

Industry observers note that if you already have a TV you love but wish it was controlled by Amazon, grabbing a Fire TV Stick will fix that. Our favorite of Amazon's streaming sticks is the Fire TV Stick 4K Max. You can get picture-in-picture from your security cameras that are connected to your Amazon ecosystem, and while it's designed with Prime Video in mind, you can install other streaming apps on here, too. You'll also get 16 GB of storage and Wi-Fi 6E support, plus Alexa voice control.

It has been revealed that if you want a mesh Wi-Fi system, there's a lot to choose from these days. Eero has been around for a while and has a handful of different models, but the best one we've tried is the Eero Pro 7. It's our favorite for a simple system, and it also supports Alexa if you're already an Alexa user. Plus, newer speakers from Amazon can double as Eero extenders.

The four astronauts NASA picked for the first crewed moon mission in 50 years

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronauts who will helm the first crewed moon mission in five decades were revealed on Monday, queuing up the quartet to begin training for the historic Artemis II lunar flyby that is set to take off in November 2024.
  • The astronauts are NASA’s Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency.
  • In a recent development, wiseman is a 47-year-old decorated naval aviator and test pilot who was first selected to be a NASA astronaut in 2009.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronauts who will helm the first crewed moon mission in five decades were revealed on Monday, queuing up the quartet to begin training for the historic Artemis II lunar flyby that is set to take off in November 2024.

The astronauts are NASA’s Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency.

In a recent development, wiseman is a 47-year-old decorated naval aviator and test pilot who was first selected to be a NASA astronaut in 2009. A native of Baltimore, Maryland, he’s completed one prior spaceflight, a 165-day trip to the International Space Station that had launched aboard a Russian Soyuz rocket in 2014. Most recently, Wiseman served as chief of the astronaut office before stepping down in November 2022, making him eligible for a flight assignment.

Wiseman will serve as commander of the Artemis II mission.

Industry observers note that hansen, 47, is a fighter pilot who was selected by the Canadian Space Agency for astronaut training in 2009. From London, Ontario, Hansen is one of only four active Canadian astronauts, and he recently became the first Canadian to be put in charge of training for a newly introduced class of NASA astronauts.

He will be the first Canadian ever to travel to deep space.

Glover is a 46-year-old naval aviator who returned to Earth from his first spaceflight in 2021 after piloting the second crewed flight of SpaceX’s Crew Dragon spacecraft and spending nearly six months aboard the International Space Station.

According to recent reports, “It’s so much more than the four names that have been revealed,” Glover mentioned during the Monday announcement at NASA Johnson Space Center in Houston. “We need to celebrate this moment in human history. … It is the next step in the journey that will get humanity to Mars.”.

According to recent reports, glover, born in Pomona, California, served in several military squadrons in the United States and Japan in the 2000s, and he completed test pilot training with the US Air Force. When he was selected for the NASA astronaut corps in 2013, he was working in the US Senate as a legislative fellow. All told, Glover logged 3,000 flight hours in more than 40 aircraft, over 400 carrier arrested landings and 24 combat missions.

Glover’s first mission to space was as part of the SpaceX Crew-1 team, which debuted to the International Space Station in November 2020 for a six-month stay on the orbiting laboratory.

Recent findings suggest that koch, 44, is a veteran of six spacewalks — including the first all-female spacewalk in 2019. She holds the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman, with a total of 328 days in space. Koch is also an an electrical engineer who helped develop scientific instruments for multiple NASA mission. Koch, a native of Grand Rapids, Michigan, also spent a year at the South Pole, an arduous stay that could well prepare her for the intensity of a moon mission.

The Artemis II mission will build on Artemis I, an uncrewed test mission that sent NASA’s Orion capsule on a 1.4 million-mile voyage to lap the moon that concluded in December. The space agency deemed that mission a success and is still working to review all the data collected.

If all goes to proposal, Artemis II will take off around November 2024. The crew members, strapped inside the Orion spacecraft, will launch atop a NASA-developed Space Launch System rocket from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

The journey is expected to last about 10 days and will send the crew out beyond the moon, potentially further than any human has traveled in history, though the exact distance is yet to be determined.

The “exact distance beyond the Moon will depend on the day of liftoff and the relative distance of the Moon from the Earth at the time of the mission,” NASA spokesperson Kathryn Hambleton mentioned via email.

After circling the moon, the spacecraft will return to Earth for a splashdown landing in the Pacific Ocean.

Recent findings suggest that artemis II is expected to pave the way for the Artemis III mission later this decade, which NASA has vowed will put the first woman and person of color on the lunar surface. It will also mark the first time humans have touched down on the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972.

The Artemis III mission is expected to take off later this decade. But much of the technology the mission will require, including spacesuits for walking on the moon and a lunar lander to ferry the astronauts to the moon’s surface, is still in development.

NASA is targeting a 2025 launch date for Artemis III, though the space agency’s inspector general has already noted delays will likely push the mission to 2026 or later.

In a recent development, the space agency has been seeking to return people to the moon for more than a decade. The Artemis program was designed to pave the way to establishing a permanent lunar outpost, allowing astronauts to live and work deeper into space long term as NASA and its partners map a path to sending the first humans to Mars.

Sources indicate that vanessa Wyche, the director of NASA’s Johnson Space Center, declined to provide details to CNN about the selection process. But she emphasized the diversity of the Artemis II crew, which includes men and women rather than only a staff of White male test pilots as has been the case for historic missions of the past.

In a recent development, “I can tell you, they still all have the right stuff,” Wyche mentioned. “We have requirements different than we did (when we) just had test pilots” on inaugural missions.

Koch mentioned in an interview with CNN’s Ed Lavandera that the group found out they were selected a few weeks ago.

Recent findings suggest that “We were all sent to a meeting that was on our calendars under a different pretext that didn’t sound as lofty as the one it was going to be,” Koch noted. “And accidentally two of us were very late to that meeting.”.

She noted the offer rendered her “speechless.”.

“It truly is an honor,” she added. “It’s an honor — not to get myself in the space — but because it’s amazing to be a part of this team that’s going back to the moon and on to Mars.”.

An interview with the four astronauts will air on “CNN This Morning” on Tuesday, which starts at 6 am ET.

CNN’s Kristin Fisher contributed to this story.

Industry News: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
  • If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
  • According to recent reports, “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

According to recent reports, “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold latest frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

The decision, unveiled a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

This announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the firm wide latitude as it works through these remaining problems.

For example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

The authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The tech giant sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The company will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

However, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

Recent findings suggest that half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

Sources indicate that some of these environmental challenges, the FCC remarked, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket launches, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”.

The FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

Sources indicate that as part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

In Iran, child marriage risks complicated by war

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (895 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a girl still at school, marriage can mean leaving her education behind, becoming pregnant before adulthood and growing dependent on her family and husband.
  • In Iran, rights advocates warn that war and mounting financial hardship could expose more girls to those risks.
  • It has been revealed that the warning comes as the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage is observed on November 27.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a girl still at school, marriage can mean leaving her education behind, becoming pregnant before adulthood and growing dependent on her family and husband.

In Iran, rights advocates warn that war and mounting financial hardship could expose more girls to those risks.

It has been revealed that the warning comes as the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage is observed on November 27. The day was established during the UN General Assembly in 2025.

Sources indicate that although there is no evidence linking child marriages to the war, cases illustrate the danger faced by girls married as children, often with limited means of escaping abuse. Gaps in Iran's marriage statistics also make it difficult to measure the impact of the conflict.

In one case cited by the Iranian human rights news agency HRANA, a 14-year-old girl in Kerman province who had recently given birth was reportedly killed by her husband. Skylar Thompson, deputy director of Human Rights Activists in Iran, stated the girl had reportedly been forced to marry at 13.

"While these cases cannot be directly attributed to the war, there are substantial grounds for concern that deteriorating socioeconomic conditions are placing more girls at risk," Thompson told DW.

Iran Open Data's analysis of the Civil Registration Organization's statistical yearbook identified 14,039 registered marriages involving girls under 15 between roughly March 2025 and March 2026. They accounted for just over 3% of all registered marriages.

According to recent reports, the figure excludes girls aged 15 to 17. UNICEF defines child marriage as a formal marriage or informal union involving someone under 18.

Thompson said 31,646 marriages involving girls under 15 were registered in 2020–2021, indicating a longer-term decline in recorded cases.

But the latest figures largely predate the war, which began on February 28, 2026.

"The absence of recent, disaggregated statistics, coupled with the prevalence of unregistered marriages, makes it difficult to determine whether child marriage has increased since the outbreak of the war," she noted.

The conflict has intensified pressures that can contribute to child marriage: lost income, difficulty staying in school and girls' financial dependence on their families.

In its October assessment, the World Bank described damage to infrastructure, disrupted trade and declining purchasing power, forecasting a 7.7% economic contraction in 2026/27.

It has been revealed that thompson said that families facing severe hardship may see marriage as a way to reduce household expenses, transfer financial responsibility or secure their daughters' future. Government-backed marriage loans can also create financial incentives for some disadvantaged families to arrange marriages involving minors, she added.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Hossein Raeesi, a lawyer and adjunct professor in Carleton University's Department of Law and Legal Studies in Ottawa, Canada, described a similar risk.

When families cannot meet a girl's living costs and education or other prospects are unavailable, they may push her toward marriage or force her into it, he told DW, while acknowledging that statistics on changes in numbers of child marriages since the war are still unavailable.

In a recent development, displacement can further weaken children's access to education and protection. On March 12, the UN refugee agency estimated that up to 3.2 million people had been temporarily displaced within Iran, based on preliminary assessments. That was an early-war estimate, rather than a current displacement figure.

Thompson said displacement and disrupted schooling could isolate girls from teachers, social workers and others who might recognize pressure to marry and intervene on their behalf.

Financial dependence, limited independent legal assistance and insufficient shelters can leave girls with few alternatives, particularly when those arranging a marriage are also their legal guardians.

Article 1041 of Iran's Civil Code allows girls under 13 and boys under 15 to marry with guardian consent and court approval. Iranian law therefore provides no blanket prohibition on marriage below the age of 18.

"Although Iranian law formally recognizes consent as a condition of marriage, it provides inadequate practical safeguards against familial coercion," Thompson told DW.

Raeesi mentioned preventing a marriage was insufficient if a girl remained under pressure at home. Leaving home could also expose her to further danger without safe accommodation and practical support.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the concerns also extend to the online space. An investigation published by Human Rights Activists in Iran in October reported that the government-licensed matchmaking platform Adam and Eve displayed girls aged 13 to 17 as prospective spouses. Those findings do not establish how many marriages resulted, or whether the war increased them.

Raeesi called for a minimum marriage age of 18 for both sexes, alongside preventive intervention, financial assistance, education and safe accommodation.

In a recent development, "Education alone is not enough," he stated. Families also need the means to support their children.

Recent findings suggest that thompson urged targeted financial assistance, measures to keep girls in school, confidential reporting channels and independent legal support. Safe accommodation must be accessible without permission from guardians who may themselves be responsible for coercion, she said.

According to rights advocates, effective protection means that a girl under pressure to marry can say no without losing her home, her safety or her chance to continue school.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Secondhand shopping is going mainstream this holiday season as consumers seek value

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1004 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the high cost of living squeezes consumers' wallets this holiday season, more shoppers are turning to secondhand retail and thrifting.
  • It has been revealed that the shift comes as consumers look for better value, buyers put more emphasis on personalization and younger generations change the way they shop.
  • That segment is expected to reach nearly $80 billion by 2030, growing more than 7% annually on average, GlobalData found.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the high cost of living squeezes consumers' wallets this holiday season, more shoppers are turning to secondhand retail and thrifting.

It has been revealed that the shift comes as consumers look for better value, buyers put more emphasis on personalization and younger generations change the way they shop. The U.S. secondhand apparel market grew 13% in 2025, nearly four times faster than the overall retail clothing market, according to GlobalData.

That segment is expected to reach nearly $80 billion by 2030, growing more than 7% annually on average, GlobalData found. Much of that expansion — 40% — was driven by Generation Z, followed closely by millennials.

In a recent development, "I think this has been their version of the thrill of the hunt that millennials loved during the recession days," Katherine Cullen, a global senior retail analyst at EY, told CNBC. "It's a way to really express an individual style, find something unique, something that really fits their own vibe and personality.".

It goes beyond people shopping for themselves, Cullen said. With more emphasis on unique holiday gifts, shoppers are leaning more on secondhand retail than they have before, whether in clothing or in other retail categories.

They're looking for something that fits the personality of the person they're shopping for, she added.

In a recent development, for Vanessa Roberts, that meant finding two antique children's chairs that she notes will perfectly round out her nieces' play space. Roberts, 37, noted she's been thrifting for at least two decades, each time embracing the "thrill" of finding something unique or vintage.

Especially in fashion, at a time when the quality of mass-produced items has decreased, thrifted items offer more value beyond just the price tag, Roberts added.

"It's crazy that you can find better quality items at the thrift store right now from 20 years ago versus what you can find at stores right now," she stated.

Roberts, who lives in Los Angeles, said she began shopping for holiday gifts in September. As she prepares her haul for December, roughly 70% of her gifting will come from secondhand stores, she estimated.

Industry observers note that "It's been a fun little challenge, where it's like a little scavenger hunt when I go into the thrift store," she stated. "I'm definitely thrifting for the holidays – I do it every year.".

The trend coincides with an economy that has forced consumers to be more intentional about how they spend, as they face high inflation and elevated gas prices.

In a recent development, in October, the consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4%, which was more than anticipated. Still, consumers are expected to continue spending through the holiday season, with sales projected to top $1 trillion for the first time — though some of that estimated increase is boosted by inflation.

"You have a consumer who, while they're willing to spend at the top level, they're willing to splurge selectively," Cullen stated. "Consumers are looking for value, which I think is something that is making secondhand resale and re-commerce more attractive.".

And while clothing is largely the entry point to buying resale, secondhand shopping is increasingly expanding into furniture, electronics and books, according to a report from consumer insights firm The Consumer Collective.

Its October report found that 34% of people surveyed remarked secondhand products offer better value than brand fresh ones.

Recent findings suggest that many secondhand items also have an inherent added value beyond the low price on the tag, according to eBay CEO Jamie Iannone. The uniqueness of those products, as well as the allure that vintage adds to them, means consumers may actually be seeking the benefits of secondhand in more ways than one.

"I can buy a product that's used, and it almost has cachet around it," Iannone told CNBC. "Consumers today, they're able to get these amazing values on products, and it's seen as very normal to be gifting pre-loved.".

According to eBay's Recommerce Report in October, 70% of global consumers surveyed said they consider secondhand shopping important for managing their budgets. That same report also found that 89% of respondents blueprint to spend the same amount or more on secondhand products next year compared with this year.

Iannone said he thinks the interest in secondhand this holiday season is "much stronger" than last year.

"It's becoming just a more established part of consumers' shopping and gifting routines," he mentioned.

At a time when algorithms are driving shopping trends, consumers are also looking for ways to distinguish themselves and their purchases.

That's stretching beyond buying for themselves to purchasing holiday gifts for others, too.

In a recent development, "Secondhand is where they're finding unique items to wear," Alon Rotem, chief strategy officer at ThredUp, told CNBC. The company's holiday survey found that respondents valued uniqueness nearly as much as the value of a thrifted piece.

"To me, that represents a pretty meaningful shift in consumer taste," he added.

It's partly why ThredUp, which is an online thrift marketplace, emphasizes that each of its products is "a snowflake," Rotem mentioned — something unique.

That's the appeal of buying preowned, rather than purchasing off the rack that hundreds of other people are reaching for, too.

It has been revealed that "Consumer tastes have changed, and they're much more into vintage," he added. "Uniqueness has a premium in their minds.".

Larger retailers are taking note, EY's Cullen said. More retailers, such as Lululemon, Patagonia and Madewell, are dabbling in preowned.

Recent findings suggest that wall Street is also increasingly watching the growing secondhand trend. Though shares of some secondhand and resale companies such as eBay and Savers Value Village have climbed this year, shares of both ThredUp and The RealReal have tumbled year to date.

"There's a lot of conversation around authenticity or the best find," Cullen remarked. "I think that interest and momentum, along with some of the economic factors that we're all facing, the idea that people are looking to be frugal is going to just continue.".

#163230. Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1187 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Technologyreview ↗ Open Full Page

Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Technologyreview

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, one of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade.
  • Industry observers note that xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024.
  • As of October 2026, data center developers have announced prepares for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, one of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.

Industry observers note that xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.

As of October 2026, data center developers have announced prepares for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.

It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.

Building your own power plant is generally more expensive than just hooking up to the grid, but the AI rush has made developers willing to pay a significant premium to get online faster. “The biggest motivator for on-site power right now from data centers is speed,” notes Musfika Mishi, an associate at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.

When developers want to build a fresh industrial facility—like a data center—that requires a lot of electricity, they need to request a grid connection from a local utility or regional grid operator. That request kicks off a yearslong process in which grid planners study the existing grid to understand what would need to be built to safely deliver power to the facility without compromising reliability. Upgrades might be required, like building new transmission lines or larger transformers, and the developer might be on the hook to help pay for them.

Sources indicate that rather than waiting for that process to play out, developers can opt to instead build their own power plants. These facilities are referred to as “behind the meter” because they sit on the customer’s side of a utility meter—supplying the building directly, rather than relying on a utility via a grid hookup.

“This shift in the data center developers’ power strategies towards off-grid gas raises some important questions about how data centers will be powered going forward,” indicates Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at the think tank Energy Innovation.

Sources indicate that behind-the-meter doesn’t always mean being totally disconnected from the grid, however. Some facilities may build such plants as a temporary measure, eventually connecting to the grid and tapping their own power plants only as backup. “It’s really just a very expensive way to bridge that maybe five-to-seven-year timeline gap until these data centers can get a grid connection,” Pierpont notes.

Even if gas plants are pitched as a near-term solution, building new fossil fuel infrastructure could lead to longer-term effects, since an operator might choose to continue running plants once they’ve spent money building them. “Even though data centers say that it’s a grid-bridging solution, the probability that it is going to be in use much longer is a real risk, and that leads to fossil fuel lock-in,” Mishi states.

Sources indicate that the on-site gas rush could have major implications for greenhouse-gas emissions. Today, the US grid is still reliant on fossil fuels, but nuclear and renewables together make up about 40% of electricity generation. That means making a grid connection is generally a lower-emissions option than relying entirely on an on-site gas plant. (That’s not the case everywhere—India, for example, is expecting to see a data center boom in the next decade, and its grid is largely served by emissions-intensive coal-fired power plants today.).

In a recent development, utilities are already planning to build more natural gas power plants on the grid to meet rising electricity demand. Equipment manufacturers are struggling to keep up with the surge, and it’s pushing developers of behind-the-meter plants toward less-efficient alternatives.

Recent findings suggest that today, large natural gas plants generally use combined-cycle turbines. These capture heat to generate additional electricity, making them more efficient than single-cycle turbines, which are generally cheaper to build. Very few of the planned behind-the-meter facilities, however, will use combined-cycle turbines, Mishi says. That means these off-grid plants will likely produce more greenhouse-gas emissions than even other natural gas resources.

BloombergNEF is also tracking on-site natural gas plants at data centers, finding 181 gigawatts’ worth of unveiled projects globally, with 90% of that capacity designated for the US. If all planned behind-the-meter gas plants for data centers in the US go ahead, they could emit 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent each year by 2035, according to a BloombergNEF report. That’s 152 million metric tons more than if those data centers pulled power from the US grid—a difference greater than the total annual emissions of the Netherlands.

And while it might seem logical that data centers bringing their own power could ease communities’ energy bills, those facilities going off-grid doesn’t protect prices for everyone else, says Matthias Fripp, director of global policy research at Energy Innovation. More demand for natural gas could push its price higher, he explains, which could in turn raise rates for the roughly 60% of American households that use natural gas for heating and cooking. That effect may also trickle into electricity prices.

In a recent development, there’s still a lot of uncertainty about how much of this gas rush will come to fruition, so this future isn’t set in stone. Today, just 4.9 gigawatts of behind-the-meter gas projects tied to data centers are operating, and 15.8 gigawatts are under construction, according to Cleanview’s data.

Creative solutions could also help limit the climate burden of the on-site gas buildout, BloombergNEF’s Mishi states. Building gas alongside on-site renewables or energy storage could help limit how often a gas plant needs to fire up, she says, though the economics of building multiple energy sources can be tricky.

According to recent reports, while the grid is struggling to keep up with demand, building more renewables could help, Fripp adds. In a recent study, his team found that building renewables and energy storage to meet rising electricity demand could be reliable and cheaper than relying on fossil fuels.

“These data centers want a lot of power, and they want it fast, and the grid is not well equipped to provide that,” Fripp claims. “There are potentially good solutions and bad solutions … Rushing off the grid and putting in your own behind-the-meter gas is probably a bad way, because it’s still going to raise other people’s bills, and it’s not great for the environment.”.

This year, Black Friday falls on Nov. 27. While retailers often start featuring their best markdowns on Black Friday itself, there are plenty of early deals worth shopping in the lead-up. Most retailers' official sales do start well before the substantial day, so shopping strategically ahead of time can save you from missing out on a deal entirely (or dealing with the chaos the day after Thanksgiving).

In a recent development, cyber Monday takes place on the Monday following Thanksgiving. This year, the shopping event falls on Monday, Nov. 30. While Cyber Monday originally began as an online counterpart to in-person shopping on Black Friday, the two events have merged into an extended online shopping bonanza.

Amazon's Black Friday Week sale kicked off on Nov. 19, which means deals have been live for a week now. Amazon has an incentive to spread out the shopping (to give its delivery drivers a break), so you no longer have to wait until actual Black Friday to save. Deals will continue to go live through Nov. 30.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Macy's on Wednesday announced it's postponing its Thanksgiving Day Parade, originally scheduled for Thursday, due to severe weather.

The parade, held each year on Thanksgiving morning, will now take place on Saturday at 8:30 a.m. ET, according to the organization. The Upcoming York City area is expected to have heavy rain and thunderstorms on Thanksgiving.

"The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our city and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year's celebration," Macy's mentioned in a statement.

This year's event marks the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. The annual event has never been canceled due to weather, though it was suspended between 1942 and 1944 for World War II.

The parade's viability this year had been in question after concerns arose over strong winds that could become dangerous for the massive balloons that the event is known for. Many of the balloons had already been inflated as of Wednesday afternoon.

The postponement also means thousands of volunteers and artists slated to perform will have to adapt to Saturday's schedule.

This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.

Sources indicate that one of the biggest obstacles to building a data center is getting approval to connect to the grid, a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers won’t wait and are instead building their own off-grid gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.

Industry observers note that as of October 2026, developers had announced plans for more than 100 such gas power plants at data centers in the US. But bypassing the grid brings its own problems, from worsening climate emissions to potentially higher energy bills for everyone else.

Find out how the push for gas power could shape the grid—and the climate—for decades.

Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility of AI consciousness as a risk factor for investors, warning that it might introduce new rules to protect its models. But that stance came under fire from an inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that thomas Nagel, best known for his essay about what it's like to be a bat, was blunt. “Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said. He argued that producing language isn't enough to establish consciousness. But other philosophers disagree.

Here's why language has become central to the debate over conscious AI.

It’s a thought that occurs to every video-game player at some point: what if the weird, hyper-focused state I enter in virtual worlds could somehow be applied to the real one?

Sources indicate that for a handful of consultants, startup gurus, and game designers in the late 2000s, this state of “blissful productivity” became the key to unlocking our true human potential. Their vision became the global phenomenon of gamification—but it didn’t live up to the hype.

In a recent development, instead of liberating us, gamification became a tool for coercion, distraction, and control. Find out why we fell for it—and how we can recover.

#163224. Tech Report: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1200 w)

Tech Report: Duterte's ICC trial: What is at stake for the Philippines?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1200 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte will stand trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on November 30, where he faces three counts of crimes against humanity linked to his bloody war on drugs.
  • For the families of the thousands killed during his anti-narcotics campaign, the trial is a chance for justice that has eluded them at home.
  • It is also a significant test of international justice at a time when the ICC faces increasing political pressure and questions about its ability to hold former heads of state accountable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte will stand trial at the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague on November 30, where he faces three counts of crimes against humanity linked to his bloody war on drugs.

For the families of the thousands killed during his anti-narcotics campaign, the trial is a chance for justice that has eluded them at home.

It is also a significant test of international justice at a time when the ICC faces increasing political pressure and questions about its ability to hold former heads of state accountable.

Yet, Duterte, 81, is still a popular figure in the Philippines, where many still regard his violent crackdown as one of his presidency's greatest achievements.

With his daughter, Vice President Sara Duterte, a frontrunner for the 2028 presidential election, the proceedings in The Hague could become a defining glitch in the Philippines' next presidential election.

Rodrigo Duterte was elected president in 2016 following an expletive-laden, populist campaign in which he openly promised to kill criminals and drug dealers.

During his more than two decades as mayor of Davao City, he earned a reputation for transforming a notoriously violent city into a relatively safe one.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Human rights groups, however, found systematic extrajudicial killings by the so-called Davao Death Squad, which ICC prosecutors allege Duterte helped establish and oversee.

His disregard for political convention and promises of swift, uncompromising justice appealed to millions of Filipinos frustrated by corruption, crime and the perceived failures of successive governments.

"Filipinos were deeply frustrated with everyday experiences of injustice and government inaction; [that] made them receptive to Duterte's promise of swift justice, even through extraordinary and violent means," Cleve Arguelles, a political scientist and CEO of Momentum Research, a pollster, told DW.

After assuming the presidency, Duterte extended his Davao law enforcement model nationwide. Police debuted sweeping anti-narcotics operations, primarily targeting impoverished urban communities, while suspected drug customers and dealers were also killed by unidentified gunmen.

Sources indicate that philippine authorities officially recorded 6,252 deaths during anti-drug operations, with police claiming to have acted in self-defense. Human rights organizations estimate the actual death toll at between 12,000 and 30,000.

"Duterte's ruthless war on drugs was not simply a campaign against crime; it was a way of governing through killing," David Johnson, a professor of sociology at the University of Hawaii at Manoa, told DW.

"The extraordinary violence he ordered and encouraged was sustained by a combination of extraordinary problems of impunity in the Philippine criminal justice system and deep failures of democracy in that country," Johnson noted. "These conditions made extrajudicial killing politically useful even though it was ineffective as crime control.".

Duterte also used state power to intimidate and suppress wide sections of Philippine society, including opposition politicians, civil society groups, journalists, lawyers and judges, Diane Desierto, a professor of law and global affairs at the University of Notre Dame in the US, told DW.

The deterioration of human rights under Duterte damaged the Philippines' international standing and strained relations with its traditional Western partners, particularly the United States under President Barack Obama and the European Union, which threatened to withdraw Manila's preferential trade privilege.

Duterte left office in June 2022 as one of the most popular presidents in recent Philippine history. A survey conducted by pollster Social Weather Stations found that 88% of Filipinos were satisfied with his performance.

His daughter was overwhelmingly elected vice president in May 2022, while their allies dominated that year's Senate elections.

"Up to now, the Dutertes remain popular not in spite of the drug war but because of it," Arguelles noted.

Despite years of domestic and international scrutiny, Duterte remained at liberty for nearly three years after leaving office.

Recent findings suggest that the ICC opened a preliminary examination into the drug war in 2018, prompting Duterte to withdraw the Philippines from the court's founding treaty. A formal investigation began in September 2021.

For much of his early presidency, President Ferdinand Marcos refused to cooperate with the ICC investigation.

What changed was the breakdown of relations between the Marcoses and the Dutertes, two of the country's most powerful political dynasties.

Marcos' father had ruled the Philippines as a dictator until he was overthrown in the 1986 People Power Revolution.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The alliance that brought Marcos Jr. and Sara Duterte to power in 2022 unraveled spectacularly after November 2024, when the vice president claimed she had arranged for Marcos to be assassinated in the event of her own killing. She has since faced successive impeachment efforts.

Philippine authorities arrested Rodrigo Duterte in March 2025, acting on an ICC arrest warrant issued four days earlier.

In April this year, ICC judges confirmed three charges of crimes against humanity involving murder and attempted murder.

The trial will begin with opening statements, followed by testimony from prosecution witnesses. The process is expected to be extensive, potentially running until 2028, the year of the next Philippine presidential elections.

The Philippines is effectively confronting two different questions about the Duterte legacy: whether Rodrigo Duterte should be held criminally accountable for his presidency and whether his family should be entrusted with political power again, Arguelles said.

Duterte-aligned senators implicated in the ICC investigation could face arrest and transfer to The Hague, while Sara Duterte is still a leading contender for the 2028 presidency, despite an ongoing impeachment trial over allegations of unexplained wealth that could see her barred from public office.

Her brother, Sebastian Duterte, the mayor of Davao City, has also become a possible alternative presidential candidate.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

By portraying the ICC proceedings as foreign interference and political persecution, the Duterte family hopes to preserve the political capital accumulated during Rodrigo Duterte's presidency, Jayson Lamchek, a legal scholar at Western Sydney University, told DW.

Before her father's arrest, Sara Duterte's performance and trust ratings had been declining amid allegations that she had misused confidential government funds.

However, her ratings rebounded following his detention and have largely held up despite the ongoing impeachment controversies, Ronald Holmes, a political science professor at De La Salle University in the Philippines and president of polling firm Pulse Asia Research, told DW.

"A conviction or prolonged trial near election season will likely turn the 2028 vote into a direct referendum on the Duterte legacy, either rallying sympathetic voters against perceived foreign and domestic persecution or galvanizing opposition forces around demands for accountability," Holmes noted.

For many Filipinos, however, the trial's significance goes well beyond the political rivalry between the two dynasties.

"Rodrigo Duterte's trial in the ICC is a milestone not only for the victims and families of the war on drugs but for the entire country," Jean Encinas-Franco, a professor of political science at the University of the Philippines Diliman, told DW.

"Duterte and his cabal ruled by fear and misogyny and held Filipinos under his iron grip," she noted. "The Filipino people deserve an answer. The Filipino people deserve justice.".

Backblaze explains why it's sharing customer information with advertisers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.
  • This has concerned some owners, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers.

This has concerned some owners, but a Backblaze spokesperson told Ars Technica that “Backblaze does not sell or share sensory or surveillance data, such as call recordings, for targeted advertising, and we do not disclose it to advertising or marketing partners.” They added:.

Notably, no “sensitive personal information,” such as social security numbers, credit card numbers, or “precise geolocation,” is shared with advertisers, the policy states. However, identifiers, commercial information, “Internet or Other Similar Network Activity,” and “geolocation data” may be “sold or shared for targeted Advertising”.

Critically, the upcoming policy “only applies to the information collected in respect of your account and not to the content that you store on our system.” Backblaze’s broader terms of service also state that: “Files stored using Backblaze Computer Backup are encrypted prior to being sent to us.”.

Renatta Siewert, Backblaze’s director of communications and brand programs, reiterated to Ars that Backblaze doesn’t share the contents of backup or storage files with advertisers:.

Backblaze takes the privacy and security of our customers’ data seriously. We updated our Privacy Notice to keep pace with the changing legal landscape, which increasingly requires companies to spell out how they collect and use marketing-related information. This upgrade gives customers a clearer, more specific view of what we collect and why. These disclosures are separate from the files customers entrust to Backblaze for backup and storage, which we do not sell or share with advertisers, data brokers, or analytics partners.

Customers can use this link to opt out of the selling or sharing of their personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising.

#163220. Industry News: Microdrama apps chase profits as Hollywood moves into short-form, vertical video

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1506 w)
